lens: public website + infrastructure reliability + exact-head CI + CANON-007/019/031/041/045/047/048/051
primaryListVerdict: The deterministic Genius List correctly refused to call S291 remotely verified: exact-head Lighthouse and Accessibility are green, but E2E run 30173344575 is red because public-intelligence remained on S290 after S291 context advanced. The same drift reproduces locally at build-check step 2. The production site itself is serving content, while one combined 47.3% metric collapses content availability and the stale Worker telemetry route into a misleading public label. The highest-leverage arc is therefore a truth-and-release lattice: seal final committed state, dimension uptime, attest the live Worker contract, bind staged artifacts beyond SHA, and repair the startup evidence parser agents use to choose work.

items.title: Make stale derived truth impossible to push after the final write-back
items.why: S291 reported build-check 220/220 before its final context mutation, then pushed PROJECT_STATUS/HANDOFF/SIL without the dependent public-intelligence and contracts. Exact-head E2E failed and the next clean pull was red.
items.premise: The build gate already detects this drift, but the installed pre-push scanner checks content safety only; it never asks whether the final committed source graph is internally coherent.
liveEvidence: GitHub E2E run 30173344575: compliance failed at Public intelligence sync check while the browser job passed
Local npm run build:check reproduced the same failure at step 2
Regenerating public intelligence advances currentSession 290→291, SIL 999→998, and replaces the S290 handoff projection with S291
scripts/pre-push-scan.mjs has no generated-contract coherence rule
items.outcome: release confidence + information-finding: any push whose final context and public contracts disagree fails locally with exact repair commands, regardless of whether closeout autopilot or a manual final commit produced it.
items.recipe: Add a source-aware final-state coherence phase to the single-process pre-push scanner, using the existing deterministic --check generators and only activating when relevant source/derived paths are in the pushed range. Make the classifier pure and self-tested, prove the captured S290→S291 mismatch fails, and keep ordinary code-only pushes fast.

L2.recipe: Gate only source-relevant pushes and print repair commands.

L3.recipe: Cover public-intelligence, contracts, heartbeat, founder-presence, startup/session coherence, negative fixtures, and the real hook path without adding per-file process storms.

executionLog.note: Added graph-driven final-state checks to the real pre-push scanner; 16/16 pure classifier/security fixtures pass.
Source-content comparison caught an actual stale status-proof embedding during S292 before the graph was rebuilt; unrelated code selects zero evidence checks.

items.title: Separate site availability, edge liveness, and telemetry intake without hiding the outage
items.why: Every sampled content route and JSON liveness path is currently healthy, but the status page labels the combined 47.3% full-stack verdict as “Availability.” Visitors can reasonably read that as the website being down half the time.
items.premise: The history already records `down: 0` for the ongoing Worker-ingest incident and the current artifact independently exposes route, liveness, and workerIngest evidence; only the rollup and consumers collapse them.
liveEvidence: api/uptime.json: all five content routes 200, liveness 200, workerIngest 405
Recent uptime-history rows are edge-degraded with down=0
build-citation.mjs and proof-card.js repeat rollup.upPct as uptime
items.outcome: UX + trust: humans and agents see origin-content availability, current edge liveness, and telemetry-route health as separate named dimensions; the 47.3% incident signal remains visible and forceful but can no longer impersonate site availability.
items.recipe: Evolve the uptime history/rollup contract compatibly: preserve legacy full-stack upPct, add originContentPct and evidence counts derived from `down`, record livenessOk/workerIngestOk on new rows, and expose dimension-specific current/rolling states. Update status, citation, proof-card, proof-line, security posture, and contract tests with honest unknown handling for legacy rows.

L1.recipe: Rename the public label and show current worker ingest separately.

L2.recipe: Add origin-content and full-stack rollups plus consumer tests.

L3.recipe: Add dimensioned history evidence, compatibility rules, dual-audience incident copy, and every downstream trust-surface update.

executionLog.note: Preserved legacy full-stack upPct (47.3%) and added originContent, edgeLiveness, and workerIngest dimensions with evidence counts.
All 697 legacy rows derive 100% origin-content availability while legacy liveness/ingest remain unknown; consumers and 33/33 + 12/12 fixtures updated.

items.title: Publish a privacy-safe live contract receipt for the routed production Worker
items.why: The local security posture can be perfect while an out-of-band production deploy serves a different Worker. That exact blind spot left RUM, Trusted Types, and CSP-report intake dark for 23 days.
items.premise: Multiple dependency-free, non-mutating route signatures can distinguish the expected Worker from Pages fallback without changing auth state or requiring production deployment.
liveEvidence: OPTIONS /v/rum is 405 in production while the repository Worker contract is 204
api/security-posture.json is source-derived and therefore cannot prove the routed Worker
probe-uptime checks only one Worker-specific route
The release lattice already consumes compact public receipts
items.outcome: security + information-finding: one deterministic receipt says which expected edge contracts are source-present, live-observed, mismatched, or unverified, with no tokens, user data, or destructive probes; status and release proof stop treating local Worker code as production evidence.
items.recipe: Create an import-safe probe/renderer for bounded OPTIONS/GET contracts (`/_health`, `/v/rum`, `/v/tt-report`, `/v/csp-report`, anonymous auth/session endpoints where safe). Store only status, expected status, latency, reason code, and source-contract hash. Add pure fixtures, privacy validation, status-proof/release-proof/security-posture integration, and an honest-dark network failure path.

L2.recipe: Probe the bounded route family and validate privacy.

L3.recipe: Bind source contract hashes, integrate release/security/status truth, and prove mismatch/unreachable/healthy fixtures.

executionLog.note: Published a five-route, SHA-256 source-bound, privacy-safe receipt with 6/6 healthy/mismatch/unreachable/privacy fixtures.
Live probes found 0/5 expected routes—two Pages-style 404s and three OPTIONS 405s—with no bodies or credentials retained; integrated across status/release/security.

items.title: Bind staging readiness to the critical artifact set, not only the candidate SHA
items.why: Exact-SHA equality prevents an old candidate from passing, but it does not prove that every critical route, shell, proof feed, and agent manifest is complete or byte-consistent on the deployed origin.
items.premise: The repository already has a current runtime candidate and canonical staging currently reports a build-SHA mismatch, clearing S290's “next runtime candidate” activation gate.
liveEvidence: Critical artifacts already have deterministic bytes and bounded public paths
S291's stale public-intelligence failure demonstrates that one commit can contain an incomplete derived set even when its SHA is exact
items.outcome: release confidence + agent discovery: a compact manifest proves the critical route/content set expected for one candidate, and staging parity reports missing, mismatched, extra-critical, or unobserved artifacts without exposing private files.
items.recipe: Build a deterministic SHA-256 Merkle manifest over a curated critical public set (shell manifest, status/release/identity/authority feeds, agents.json, llms entrypoint, key route HTML). Include leaf path/hash/bytes, domain-separated tree root, candidate SHA, schema/version, and validation. Teach staging deploy to publish it and parity to compare the live manifest/root before candidateReady.

L1.recipe: Hash a fixed critical file list into one receipt.

L2.recipe: Add domain-separated Merkle construction and local validation.

L3.recipe: Publish through atomic staging, compare live leaves/root, integrate release proof, and test tamper/missing/order invariants.

executionLog.note: Built a deterministic domain-separated SHA-256 Merkle tree over 24 critical artifacts; 6/6 tamper/order/missing fixtures pass.
Parity and release proof bind candidate/served roots and cardinality.
Atomic Hetzner staging deployed 4,235 files with rollback; candidate/deployed SHA match and 24-leaf Merkle root 54be00b11438 matches exactly; --require-green passed.

items.title: Make the startup brief parse the current SIL and evidence semantics it displays
items.why: The founder-facing brief currently forecasts 0/1000 while saying every category is stable, labels current failing verification as “Where we left off,” and attributes the sibling-lock doctor warning to self.
items.premise: The SIL forecaster only parses an obsolete numbered table shape, while current SIL v3 rows are `| Category | Score | Notes |`; the renderer also mixes live build diagnostics into a previous-session block.
liveEvidence: docs/STARTUP_BRIEF.md renders Projected 0/1000 (↓998) and “All categories forecast stable or rising”
scripts/lib/sil-forecaster.mjs row regex requires a leading numeric column absent from S289-S291
The latest failed audit run correctly changes measured tests to 1/2, but the block title remains Session 291 history
Doctor source reports one sibling-lock advisory, while the brief says one self warning
items.outcome: agent UX + token reduction: the orientation brief becomes internally self-validating, distinguishes last-closeout evidence from live verification, and no longer sends the next agent into false score recovery or self-debt investigation.
items.recipe: Extract a pure startup evidence adapter, support both legacy numbered and current SIL v3 tables, require ten scored categories before forecasting, split “last closeout” from “current verification,” and derive doctor ownership from the live check vector. Add fixtures for S290/S291, zero-category refusal, partial build diagnostics, and sibling-only warnings.

L2.recipe: Add both SIL shapes and refuse partial forecasts.

L3.recipe: Add the pure evidence adapter, semantic block split, doctor ownership, and regression fixtures.

executionLog.note: Current and legacy SIL fixtures parse all ten categories and incomplete ledgers refuse forecasting (4/4).
Pure closeout/live-test/doctor-ownership adapters pass 3/3; brief splits LAST CLOSEOUT from CURRENT VERIFICATION and forecasts a real total.
